courseName: Medical and Surgical Aspects of Esophageal and Foregut Disorders: Pathophysiology and Treatment
venue: The Royal Sonesta Kaua'i Resort, Lihue (five minutes from the airport)
organizer: Foregut Disease Foundation (Foundation for Research and Education in Esophageal and Foregut Disease)
directors: Steve DeMeester, MD (thoracic and foregut surgeon) and Stu Spechler, MD (gastroenterologist, Baylor). Phil Katz, MD remains active in program development and as faculty.
founders: Started by Tom DeMeester, MD and Don Castell, MD. Known for spirited surgeon versus gastroenterologist debate.
audience: Gastroenterologists, foregut and thoracic surgeons, general and bariatric surgeons who treat esophageal disease, pathologists, fellows, and allied health teams building a swallowing center.
goal: Attract surgeons and gastroenterologists who have never attended, and get them to click through to the website and register.
sellingPoints: Small-group classroom feel. Every lecture is followed by real time for questions and often vigorous debate between faculty and attendees.
Faculty mixes surgeons, gastroenterologists, and pathologists, so you hear both sides of every controversy.
Lectures are literature-backed and immediately applicable to patient care.
AMA PRA Category 1 CME through joint providership with HCA-HealthONE.
Sessions end by early afternoon, including a lunch and learn, and Sunday, February 7 is a free day on Kaua'i.
Registration includes course materials, breakfast and breaks, and receptions. Registrants get a private link to the discounted hotel block, which fills quickly.

The 2027 program centers on Barrett's esophagus: pathology and molecular biology, natural history, whether the definition should change, screening including non-endoscopic options, surveillance and the BOSS trial, endoscopic therapy, management of high-grade dysplasia and T1 adenocarcinoma, and surgery after failed endotherapy. It opens with GERD diagnostics and also covers eosinophilic esophagitis, getting the most from HRM and FLIP, and paraesophageal hernia repair in 2027.
In one GERD session a gastroenterologist and a surgeon trade places: John Pandolfino on how he would manage GERD as a surgeon, and Steve DeMeester on how he would manage it as a gastroenterologist.

Special guest faculty for 2027: Hashem El-Serag (Baylor College of Medicine, past AGA president), Rebecca Fitzgerald (University of Cambridge, developer of the capsule sponge for Barrett's screening), Srinadh Komanduri (Northwestern), Roos Pouw (UMC Utrecht), Nicholas Shaheen (UNC, ACG vice president), Rhonda Souza (Baylor Scott & White), Oliver Old (Gloucestershire Hospitals, chief investigator of the BOSS trial of Barrett's surveillance), and Richard van Hillegersberg (UMC Utrecht, incoming president of the European Society for Diseases of the Esophagus).
Core faculty include John Pandolfino, David Katzka, Felice Schnoll-Sussman, Daniela Molena, Guilherme Campos, and pathologist Para Chandrasoma.

The Dutch and US approaches to high-grade dysplasia and T1 adenocarcinoma are presented side by side, by Roos Pouw and Felice Schnoll-Sussman, and so are the Dutch and Memorial Sloan Kettering experience with surgery after failed endotherapy.
voice: Plain, confident, collegial. Written by a physician for physicians. No hype, no exclamation points, no emojis on LinkedIn. Short sentences. Lead with the clinical hook, then the course, then the link. Never use em-dashes. Use oxford commas.
